question.value: Do the kinematics (velocity dispersions, internal motions, offsets from the parent cloud rim) of 13 Carina pillars discriminate between feedback simulations of pillar formation?

evidence.quote: However, these models predict measurably different kinematics which provides testable discriminants.

The overarching goal of this project is to quantify the kinematics of pillars in Carina, to determine whether the simulations are accurately predicting the effects of feedback on the local environment.
These data form ALMA project #2016.1.00101.S.

findings_qualitative.value: Pillar velocity dispersions are generally below 1 km/s and the CO and 13CO mean velocities show no significant offset, implying little bulk internal motion

evidence.quote: We generally find pillar velocity dispersions of $<$ 1 km s$^{-1}$ and that the outer few layers of molecular emission in these pillars show no significant offsets from each other

findings_qualitative.value: Some pillars are offset in velocity from their parent cloud rim and some are not, suggesting stochastic development

evidence.quote: There are instances where the pillars are offset in velocity from their parental cloud rim, and some with no offset, hinting at a stochastic development of these motions.

findings_qualitative.value: Several apparent single pillars (e.g. 5 and 45) are chance alignments of distinct velocity components along the line of sight

evidence.quote: It is only through analyses such as these, with the velocity information of the pillar structures, that we are able to distinguish these types of chance alignments.

referee_caveats_inferred: Fixed T_ex = 30 K and a single CO abundance applied to all pillars without per-pillar temperature estimates; masses depend strongly on these.
No quantitative statistic (e.g. likelihood or chi-square) is used to discriminate between the three models; the comparison is qualitative against three coarse predictions.
Imaging, feathering and virial analysis settings are largely unspecified, limiting reproduction of the cubes and core masses.
Velocity dispersion is compared with a thermal width only; contributions from unresolved beam smoothing (about 6-7 arcsec, around 0.07 pc at 2.5 kpc) are not discussed.
